patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a compact control in the top navigation area consistent with a search field; the reference HTML also includes a search input in the header navigation.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should support text entry and search submission, likely from the header on both viewports. On mobile it may need to expand or receive focus cleanly within constrained space.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not make clear whether results are live/autocomplete or only submitted on enter/button.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch places a thin horizontal navigation row across the very top, visually separated from the article body, suggesting a persistent utility/header bar while long content scrolls below.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If implemented as persistent while scrolling, it should remain accessible and not obscure content. Active/focused items should remain usable as the page scrolls.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show scrolling states, so persistence is inferred from the detached top utility-nav layout.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a mostly static content-heavy article page with minimal JavaScript. The only clearly supported interactive requirement across both views is header search behavior. Desktop additionally suggests a utility/header navigation that may remain fixed during scrolling, but there is no strong evidence of menus, accordions, tabs, modals, or dynamic loading. Cross-viewport differences appear to be primarily layout-related rather than interaction-rich.
